name: Kahua
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 sources.bib; ABVD (lexibank/abvd); StressTyp2 2015 dump; Grambank; HathiTrust full index.
sources.note: Glottolog Kahua refs = Bruns n.d., Fox 1919 (JRAI 49, ethnographic), Tryon & Hackman 1983, Kahua Catholic Bible 2011; ABVD Kahua lists all from Tryon & Hackman; StressTyp2 lists agw with no entry; Grambank has no kahu1241; HathiTrust has no Kahua-language item.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (English), 'Owa language', revision 1298528743 (2025-07-03), section 'Stress', citing Mellow 2013 [=2014]:5.
sources.note: Second-hand for the sister lect OWA (owaa1237), not Kahua: 'Usually, the second-to-last syllable is stressed in the Owa language, e.g., auragi /ɐʊ.ˈɾɐ.gɪ/.. But occasionally the antepenultimate.. fefene /ˈfɛ.fɛ.nɛ/.. stress placement depends on the context.. difficult to predict.'

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & B. D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: KAHUA = wordlists 90 Kahua, 91 Tawaroga, 92 Mami, 93 Santa Ana, 94 Santa Catalina; sound-correspondence tables only. Vowel-reflex footnotes say 'in unstressed position' without stating where stress falls; no stress-placement statement for Kahua. Silent.

sources.citation: Naitoro, Katerina. 2019. Morphs in search of meaning: Southeast Solomonic transitive morphology in diachronic perspective. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/163714).
sources.note: Nothing on Kahua stress. Appendix A (p.355) lists the sole Kahua source as Bruns (2002), 'Grammar of the Kahua language of east and south-east Makira', unpublished ms (cited up to p.314); p.219 remarks that 'The descriptions available for SES languages rarely discuss specifics of stress assignment'.

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic languages. Richmond: Curzon (language listing).
sources.note: Kahua listed under the Makira group with no source cited (only Arosi has a sketch); nothing on Kahua stress.

sources.citation: Fox, C. E. 1924. The threshold of the Pacific: an account of the social organization, magic and religion of the people of San Cristoval. London: Kegan Paul.
sources.note: Ethnographic; pp.5-6 define the Kahua district; no phonology, no accent remark.

sources.citation: Codrington, R. H. 1885. The Melanesian languages. Oxford: Clarendon.
sources.note: San Cristoval grammars cover only Fagani and Wano (Arosi); Kahua not treated.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. Collections AC1 and AC2, PARADISEC (catalog.paradisec.org.au/collections/AC1, /AC2): Kahua materials (mission texts/grammar notes; exact items unverified -- catalogue could not be reached by automated download).
sources.note: Capell collected mission grammars and notes for Solomon Islands languages; may include a Kahua grammar or pronunciation notes (possibly Bruns' or earlier Marist material).
Nothing; only points to Capell PARADISEC collections AC1/AC2 as holding Kahua materials.

sources.citation: Bruns, Gerard. 2002 (Glottolog 569519: n.d., 76 pp.). Grammar of the Kahua language of East and South-East Makira, Solomon Islands. Unpublished manuscript (Marist mission; used by Naitoro 2019 at ANU, cited to p.314).
